- Extensive yellowing/chlorosis across the leaf
- Large brown necrotic areas that have dried out and created holes (shot-hole pattern)
- Papery, brittle texture to the necrotic tissue
- The leaf is severely damaged with large areas lost

Top candidates: Early Blight, Late Blight, Alternaria Black Molds, Septoria Leaf Blotch. Let me view reference images one at a time.
This Early Blight reference (CDDM_2508) is very similar to the test image - large brown necrotic areas with yellowing and holes in the leaf tissue. Let me check one more candidate.

Based on my analysis of the test image and 8 reference images across 6 classes:

**Test image features:**
- Tomato leaf with extensive yellowing/chlorosis
- Large brown necrotic areas, dried and papery
- Large holes where necrotic tissue fell out
- Leaf laid on white surface, severely damaged

**Key comparisons:**
- **Early Blight (CDDM_2508)**: Very close match — shows large brown necrotic patches with surrounding yellowing and holes forming as tissue drops out
- **Late Blight**: Shows large brown patches but without the yellowing halo or shot-hole pattern
- **Alternaria Black Molds**: Stem/root canker, not leaf lesions — no match
- **Septoria**: Small distinct circular spots — no match
- **Phytophthora Blight**: Stem wilting — no match
- **Tomato Spotted Wilt Virus**: Whole plant bronzing/wilting — no match

The CDDM_2508 Early Blight reference image is the closest visual match to the test image, showing the same pattern of large coalescing necrotic lesions with yellowing and loss of leaf tissue.
